newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Nine Ashes broadcast in rugby clash.
newsitem.headline: Nine Ashes broadcast in rugby clash.

text.p: Media billionaire Kerry Packer's Channel Nine television station said on Thursday it would broadcast the first session of the fourth Ashes cricket test between Australia and England on Saturday night.

Channel Nine will show the cricket in direct competition with rival free-to-air station Seven Network Ltd's live telecast of the Tri-Nations Series and Bledisloe Cup rugby union test between Australia and New Zealand in Melbourne.

Packer's Channel Nine has only once before broadcast the opening session of play in the previous three tests of the six-test series, which is tied at 1-1 ahead of the pivotal fourth test at Headingley.

Channel Nine, which is owned by Packer media group Publishing and Broadcasting Ltd, instead opted to air scheduled local programming before joining the test from the start of the second session about two hours later.
Play begins at about 8.00 p.m (1000 GMT), in favour of showing scheduled programming.
The rugby test in Melbourne, expected to be played before a record Australian crowd of about 100,000 at the Melbourne Cricket Ground, will kick off at about 8.00 p.m.

Channel Nine's programming director John Stephens said in a statement the move to show Saturday's opening session was a "one-off" move. Saturday will be the only time the first session is aired during the five-day test.
"We made a conscious decision some weeks ago to telecast live coverage of the Ashes cricket test at 8.30pm on Saturday night," Stephens said.
"(This was) because it was not pre-empting any programmes which were integral to Nine's successful program schedule."

The only other time Nine has shown the opening session was on the Saturday of the second test and gave the Australian Broadcasting Corp rights to televise the third test last month because Nine already held the Australian rights to air the Wimbledon tennis tournament.
